_comment: Retrieval arms for kgbench.
An arm is one way of answering a question. `kind: agent` spawns a headless claude
with a fixed tool surface; that surface is what distinguishes the arms, so the
comparison measures retrieval strategy rather than model.
`allowedTools` may contain the token $backendTools, which expands to the tool list
declared for that backend in config/code-graph.json. Arms must NOT hand-write MCP
tool names: deriving them is what guarantees the benchmark exercises the same tool
surface production exposes, instead of drifting from it silently.
Every arm keeps the same model and the same base prompt. Only tools differ.
TWO FURTHER AXES, both defaulting to a single value so the arm comparison stays the
controlled one it was designed to be:
agents — which coding CLI drives the cell. Defaults to claude ALONE, and that is not
timidity. Only claude accepts --allowedTools / --disallowedTools /
--strict-mcp-config, so only claude can be held to an arm's tool surface. On any
other agent the MCP servers can still be restricted but the built-in file tools
cannot, so `graphify` and `codegraph` — whose identity is having Read WITHOUT
Glob/Grep — are refused there rather than run under a label they would not honour
(lib/kgbench/agents.mjs armIsFaithful). `grep` and `hybrid` survive, because what
they withhold is MCP, which is enforceable everywhere.
models — which model each agent runs. Names are the benchmark's canonical spelling
(claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-4.6); each agent's own dialect is derived by
lib/experiments/model-resolve.mjs, since opencode wants rapid-proxy/<dotted> and
claude wants the hyphenated id.
Do NOT take the proxy's providerModels catalog as the list of usable models: it
advertises models providers reject and omits models they serve. Establish the real
list with scripts/llm-model-probe.mjs.
continuationBudget — turns an answer-file agent may spend RESUMING its own session
after finishing without writing an answer. It exists because the agents were never
getting one turn each: claude's -p loop is unbounded, copilot is launched with
--max-autopilot-continues 20, and opencode's headless `run` ends at the first
assistant step with text and no tool call — a budget of zero. Measuring one agent at
0 against another at 20 measures the harness.
DEFAULT 2, and the number is measured rather than chosen. Same 48 grep/opencode
cells at each setting (runs coding-v1-r8 and coding-v1-r8-cont2, 2026-08-10):
budget 0   6/48 answered   — run coding-v1-x2, same cells
budget 1  44/48 answered   score 0.935 on a same-denominator basis
budget 2  48/48 answered   score 0.948, wall-clock unchanged at ~46s
The decisive figure is not the completion rate but the distribution of turns spent.
At budget 1, 41 of 48 cells used the whole budget — the shape of a binding
constraint. At budget 2 the spread is 9/28/11 and NOTHING reaches the ceiling, so a
third turn would buy nothing on this question set. Raise it only against evidence of
cells pinned at 2.
Two things it is NOT. It is not a retry: a retry re-runs the question from scratch,
which for a deterministic narration-stop just narrates again (88 retries in x2 ->
88 further no-results), whereas a continuation resumes the session where the work
already happened. And it is not free accuracy — it converts unscored failures into
scored answers, some of them weak, so mean-score-over-answered FALLS (0.977 ->
0.948) while the honest same-denominator score rises. A run that quotes the first
number is quoting survivorship.
Inert for claude, whose loop is already unbounded and which has no continuation
path at all. Per-RUN, never per-agent: a per-agent budget would reintroduce exactly
the asymmetry it exists to remove. Override with --continuations.

grep.label: Agentic grep (baseline)
grep.note: No index, no infrastructure. The pattern shipping coding agents already use, and the baseline any retrieval layer has to beat.

hybrid.label: All tools, agent chooses
hybrid.note: The only production-shaped arm. Every other arm is FORCED onto one strategy, which is not how an agent actually works — so this is the number the others should be read against.
_mcpFromNote: Deliberately absent: with $allBackendTools the server list is DERIVED from the
same expansion that produced the tool names (resolveArm in lib/kgbench/arms.mjs).
Naming one backend here while granting every backend's tools is the defect that
shape invites — the unconfigured server's tools are absent rather than refused,
so the arm loses a strategy silently and still fills the table with numbers.

docs.label: Curated docs only (OKF)
docs.note: The OKF pattern: markdown + an index, no source access. Expected to win narrative/architecture questions and to be the only arm that can honestly answer 'that is not documented'.
docs.promptPrefix: You may consult ONLY files under docs/, docs-content/, and CLAUDE.md. Do not read source files. If the answer is not present in those documents, say so explicitly rather than inferring it.
